newsitem.title: USA: Westcoast still sees B.C. gas plant back Sat.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast still sees B.C. gas plant back Sat.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc's McMahon gas processing plant in British Columbia, partially shut down late Wednesday, will be operating normally on Saturday, the company said Friday.
"We're almost back to normal now. We're going to be all back to normal tomorrow," a company spokesman said, noting nominations for Saturday deliveries were being accepted.
On Thursday, the plant was operating at about 50 percent power, cutting about 325 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas flows. The plant's capacity is about 650 mmcfd.
The outage was attributed to faulty valves on the raw gas liquid receiving system.

As a result of the partial outage, prices at Sumas, Wash., the Canada/U.S. export point, surged Thursday to about $5 per million British thermal units range, as compared to the $4.00 area seen on Wednesday.
